headline: Roman has lost 8.6% of his body weight in about 12 weeks and has had new evening confusion since late October, including a stove left on. He also needs more help with bathing.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 2026-09-05 to 75.2 kg on 2026-11-24 (-7.1 kg, -8.6%), with a drop at each reading (79.8 kg on 10/01, 77.3 kg on 10/28). On 11/24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. Plan: oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights, dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record has all four weights and the -7.1 kg (-8.6%) change. The dietitian note on 11/24 matches the appetite, breakfast, 50% lunch and plan details. The note rounds the loss to 9%, which is consistent.

items.statement: On 2026-11-09 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. He was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit that week. The records show no encounters since 09/01, and no results or follow-up are documented.
items.verifier_note: The note supports the two weeks of evening confusion, the stove, orientation, no fever and the plan. The empty encounters record supports the statement that no encounters or follow-up are documented. The note names Linda but never says she is his niece, so that relationship is not supported by the cited sources.

items.statement: On 2026-09-18 Roman needed hands-on help getting out of the tub and said he had been skipping showers because he fears slipping. On 09/25 the OT found he now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing (independent at last review). The OT recommended a tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing. The notes do not show whether these were put in place.
items.verifier_note: The 09/18 aide note and the 09/25 OT note support every detail, including the change from independent at last review and the three recommendations. Nothing in the cited notes shows the recommendations were implemented, as the statement says.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit planned on 11/09 completed, and what did they show? Is the evening confusion still happening?
Could the weight loss, poor appetite, and new confusion be related? Who is following up on the weekly weights, supplement, and dental check?
Have the OT's bathing equipment and added home care hours been arranged? Is anyone addressing his fear of slipping and skipped showers?

Does the 10/24 PT evaluation (gait, walker, grab bars) apply to Roman? It references the 10/19 fall, which the 10/22 and 10/25 notes say was charted in error. Does he need a separate gait or safety evaluation?
What home safety plan is needed for the stove while his evening confusion is being worked up, and what support does Linda need?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in that window, including any for chest pain, angina, COPD/bronchitis flare, or anemia-related symptoms.

Falls and near-falls: review incident reports and nursing notes for the window; note any fall-related injury, and check fall-risk screening status given knee osteoarthritis, chronic back pain, and fibromyalgia.

Medication changes since last review: list all starts, stops, and dose changes. Current active list is metoprolol succinate 100 mg, clopidogrel 75 mg, naproxen 220 mg, nitroglycerin spray PRN, and simvastatin 20 mg. Flag any new NSAID or analgesic use alongside clopidogrel, and any new opioid, muscle relaxant, or sedative use.

Medication reconciliation and adherence: check refill gaps for metoprolol, clopidogrel, simvastatin, and nitroglycerin, and confirm the patient still has unexpired nitroglycerin spray. Verify no inhaler or COPD-related medication appears on the active list despite the chronic obstructive bronchitis diagnosis, and raise this for prescriber review rather than assuming a gap.
Allergy record: the allergy list is empty. Confirm with the patient and pharmacy whether allergies are truly absent or simply undocumented.

Blood pressure trend across the window: review all recorded readings against the hypertension and ischemic heart disease history, note orthostatic readings if taken, and flag any readings outside the team's agreed parameters.
Cardiac symptoms: chest pain or angina frequency, nitroglycerin use logged, exertional dyspnea, and any cardiology follow-up or testing due.
Respiratory status: cough, sputum, dyspnea, SpO2 readings, rescue inhaler or steroid use, and any COPD-related visits or vaccinations due.

Labs due or resulted in the window: hemoglobin/CBC given anemia history and clopidogrel plus NSAID exposure, renal function given naproxen, HbA1c given prediabetes and metabolic syndrome, and lipid panel given statin therapy. Note which are overdue.

Weight and BMI trend across the window given obesity and metabolic syndrome, plus any appetite or intake changes. Review pain scores and function: ADLs, IADLs, mobility aids, knee and back pain interference, and sleep. Check cognition and mood screens (PHQ/GDS) and attendance at PACE day programming, transport issues, and caregiver or social situation changes, noting that the enrollment record has no caregiver details.

Care-plan items due in the window or before the 2026-11-30 review: goals of care, care-plan updates, reassessment dates, and any open action items from the last IDT meeting. Summarize changes for the team to discuss without recommending treatment changes.
